computers.name: Logix Aurelia

normal_view.description: Lower RAM, including CP/M page zero and application memory

organization.note: This is the normal application mapping. Within it, 7000–EFFF remains switchable in 4 KB pages. A system call can temporarily map ROM or video RAM there, preserving and later restoring any hidden RAM. F000–FFFF remains common system RAM.
organization.dma_addressing: Physical bank selections are latched per transfer; CPU mapping changes cannot redirect DMA.
organization.refresh: AION system controller refreshes all installed system DRAM independently of CPU activity.

normal_view.description: Base and expansion RAM, including CP/M page zero and application memory. The card supplies B000–EFFF.
Stable runtime entry code, system stack and critical state.

expanded_organization.note: The card fills B000–EFFF with RAM in the normal view. ROM, cartridges and video RAM use temporary overlays within 7000–EFFF; the underlying RAM retains its contents.
expanded_organization.dma_addressing: Physical bank selections are latched per transfer; CPU mapping changes cannot redirect DMA.
expanded_organization.refresh: AION system controller refreshes all installed system DRAM independently of CPU activity.

physical_population.status: Accepted chip-count baseline; decode/refresh/electrical qualification pending.
physical_population.mapping_note: Existing mapper and common-system-RAM reservations remain unchanged; physical bank/page decode must implement the logical normal view.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 16 KiB display DRAM. The exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM remains available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 2048-byte font; glyph edits affect both pages. Independent font buffering is not advertised in this baseline.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

sprites.coordinate_space: Logical mode pixels; scale together with the background. Signed 16-bit X and Y; clip at screen edges.
sprites.priority: Lower sprite number wins; all sprites overlay background/text.
sprites.registers: Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.
sprites.updates: Switch descriptor bank atomically at vertical blank. Pattern writes require scheduled access or disabling affected sprites; 1 KiB does not hold two complete pattern sets.
sprites.allocation_policy: Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.

software_compatibility.adaptive_text: Applications query usable columns/rows instead of selecting behavior from model name.
software_compatibility.native_40_column_mode: Native 40x25 and 80x25 text on both hosts; usable width depends on monitor capabilities.

manufacturing_requirements: Populate 24 system DRAMs; AION system controller owns decode and refresh
exact FDD mechanism plus a controller/data separator (not currently a named base part)
motherboard ROM capacity/package/count and cartridge connectors
AION system controller owns mapper registers/logic
clock/reset/interrupt circuitry
complete mainboard, PSU, enclosure and harnesses. Specify motherboard versus controller-chip integration.

Populate one shared Aurelia video controller and eight AION-manufactured 4116-equivalent 16Kx1 DRAMs (16 KiB). Qualify CPU arbitration at the host clock, refresh, pixel FIFO deadlines, package, rails and external video/control line drivers.

Provide three independent point-to-point FlexiBUS host ports, including connectors, transceivers, protection and power budget; qualify simultaneous keyboard, disk and printer service. Controller die count depends on ports per die.
Manufacturer/MPN or released make drawing, approved alternatives and historical supply qualification
PCB dimensions, layer stack, finish, connectors, fitted passives and reference designators
Power per rail, startup/thermal limits and region-specific power configuration
Firmware image capacity/revision, programming and verification
Assembly routing, test fixtures, cycle times, yield/rework/scrap and packout
Qualify AION 1Kx4 static cells, 250 ns cycle target, retention while powered, +5 V supply and 18-pin DIP compatibility before launch.
Test two-chip 1Kx8 sprite bus, CPU/DMA write arbitration and worst-case five-sprite overlap.
Qualify CPU bus handover at 4 and 6 MHz, bounded DMA bursts, device-ready waits, completion interrupts and abort/reset recovery.
Verify independent refresh for every installed physical bank, including hidden banks and Aurelia 16 KiB expansion; derive deadlines from qualified DRAM ordering codes.
Freeze package/pinout, external buffers, memory decode, bank-latched DMA addressing and simultaneous video/peripheral stress tests.

networking_from_ncc_1981.implementation: Optional expansion NIC and Enhanced CP/M networking upgrade from NCC 1981.
networking_from_ncc_1981.rate_policy: Firmware-enforced host ceiling; actual common network rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

computers.lifecycle_policy: From COMDEX 1979 Logix focuses new hardware development and promotion on Aurelia+. Existing Aurelia support and compatible software continue; independent manufacturers may develop Aurelia-class clones through published interfaces and appropriate software licences. No immediate withdrawal or shutdown date is imposed.

memory.reliability_policy: No parity or ECC is fitted; any future parity design requires a separate qualified BOM.
memory.video_ram_policy: 16 KiB with the 128 KiB low-density configuration; 32 KiB with the 256 KiB AION high-density configuration. Expanding a low-density machine does not automatically replace its card.

pixel_buffer.policy: FREE/FILLING/READY/READING banks; output latches and serializer. Never overwrite active bank; underrun preserves sync.

host_interface.implementation: Buffered 32-to-8-bit bridge with byte enables, staging latches and bounded READY/backpressure. Word uploads require up to four local transfers; no native 32-bit display-memory bank is claimed.

video.monitor_policy: Mono II / Color II use legacy 200-line raster profiles. No 26.88 kHz output and no Mono Pro support. CPU word size does not widen local display memory. All five sprites remain available.

sprites.coordinate_space: Logical mode pixels; scale together with the background. Signed 16-bit X and Y; clip at screen edges.

sprites.registers: Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.

sprites.allocation_policy: Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.
sprites.descriptor_allocation_note: 80 bytes of live two-bank descriptors within a 128-byte reserved area; 48 bytes padding. 640 pattern + 128 descriptor + 256 scratch bytes = 1024.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

ncc_1982_display_upgrade.policy: Optional replacement video card; existing configurations retain their installed card. Separate COMDEX high-resolution display is outside this release.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

network.qualification_status: Reuse existing network protocol/card baseline; qualify ERA² bus, DMA, drivers and rate advertisement before release.

computers.software_policy: Accepted AIONix2 ROM-backed planning baseline. Preserve documented ERA AIONix binaries through versioned compatibility; individual applications and editions require qualification. External application ROM cartridges are not added by the internal system ROM decision.
computers.monitor_and_keyboard_bundle: Not specified; do not assume included models or pricing.
manufacturing_requirements: Storage sourcing: Rodime RO202E 20 MB HDD and Shugart Associates SA450 DS/DD FDD. Preserve functional BOM sets; model, controller, rail/startup load, enclosure and formatted geometry qualification remain open. Logix assembles the mainboard, controllers, power supply, chassis and wiring set; PSU sizing awaits a complete rail budget.
